key_insight: The first U.S. CADASIL cohort shows that a single-gene small-vessel disease can be systematically characterized with harmonized clinical, cognitive, MRI, and biomarker measures to model vascular cognitive impairment and dementia.
clinical_relevance: These baseline data help define measurable disease features and progression-ready endpoints that may improve future trial design and interpretation in CADASIL and broader VCID research.
method: Cross-sectional baseline analysis from 12 U.S. sites (Oct 2022–Jan 2025).
Adults from families with documented NOTCH3 variants underwent standardized clinical, functional, MRI, genetic, and proteomic assessments.
Comparisons used Fisher exact/Kruskal-Wallis tests with multivariable adjustment for age, sex, race, and education.
evidence_signal: The analytic cohort included 343 NOTCH3 variant carriers and 116 non-carrier family controls, with participants centrally stratified into low-, medium-, and high-risk CADASIL tiers.
watch_item: Baseline, cross-sectional findings do not establish progression or treatment response, and some enrolled participants had variants of unknown significance or pending genetic interpretation.
paper_title: The United States CADASIL Consortium: Baseline Findings from a Natural History Study
